questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- The nature and environment in the country.
- That it was a partner university so I was sure the educational standards were the same as my home country.
- New culture I could experience 
- Good recommendations of the destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had the best experience in Ljubljana! I already miss it and will forever cherish this ERASMUS experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was sent to me by E-mail with details.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were given a personal student tutor who could help with any questions and/or recommendations and you could always get help and information from the International Office at the faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult to find housing in the beginning. But I made a FB post with a picture and got  many messages from people. But be sure not to be scammed and do not send a deposit before arrival. A real landlord understands the importance of you arriving to the apartment before paying.  I can definitely recommend videochatting with your landlord and see the apartment before arrival too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed it a lot. I lived in a beautiful area by the river only 10 minutes on bicycle from the hospital. Ljubljana is not a big city, so there is never far to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got a 1 bedroom studio and it was perfect for me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and online. Everything was sent to me that I needed to fill out and use for the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If I had any questions I could always contact the international office in Ljubljana and also get help from my own university (UCPH). They always responded very quickly and were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No problem. I had my clinical rotations and got signed up by the international office to the right departments and was sent a schedule with dates and departments very quickly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions, just ask for help. They respond very quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did my clinical rotations at the hospital.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. You work at the hospital and follow residents and doctors to surgeries and procedures. Learn how to do many procedures and discuss patients and cases together.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotations in surgery: Throracic Surgery and Oncology Surgery 
Clinical rotations in internal medicine: Gastroenterology and Vascular medicine
Clinical rotations in anesthesiology - Neuro surgery and more.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All my rotations went very well! Thoracic Surgery was amazing and I truly had the best mentor. They let you do a lot and assist everyday and do surturing. Oncology Surgery was also great and they put you in the programme so you know when you are assisting at a surgery. 
Also, the rotation in anesthesiology was very special and my mentor taught me a lot of procedures. Definitely recommend.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to bring your own hospital clothes and wash it yourself! It is not available at the hospital for students. So I had to purchase white scrubs in the beginning. (approximately 25 euro for doctors coat and 30 euro for clinical pants and 5xwhite basic t-shirt 25 euro)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are very similar to Denmark in prices, but going out for a beer or wine is very cheap! 2 euros for a glass of wine, same with beer most places.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Free student sport activities and yoga!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sport activities! Also had a medicine party at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Erasmus trips! They have so many great offers, such as wine tasting, cave trips and Christmas market tours to different cities and countries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can rent a car very cheap when you are a student. So drive to the Triglav national Park and go for some amazing hikes! Kranjska Gora and the area around Ratece was one of my favorite places to go. During winter season, go skiing! Also the coastal city of Piran is beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People were very welcoming and almost everyone speak English very well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You meet many new friends at the Erasmus Trips. It's also always great to grab a drink with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language was a little difficult, so communicating with the elderly (especially patients) could be difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The positive spirit and their proudness of their country and language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be active. Show your interest to the doctors and they will bring you along to everything
- Bring your scrubs from home!
- Enjoy every single day - time flies way too fast!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a small notebook that you can write your daily experiences into.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the friendships that were created.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The language. But the website
slonline.si
was a great help!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go for it and apply for exchange! You will not regret it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
